clue.text: Opening letter, account for hotel's animal

indicators.note: account standing in for hotel signals one letter group swapped in where another was

parts.note: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel's mascot creature is being accounted for on the first page of a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' tells you to put AC in place of the H in ALPHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American camelid kept for its wool, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Passage for big hill and little Dickensian in river

indicators.note: the hill and the Dickens character are placed in the river, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: Rio is Spanish and Portuguese for river, common in crosswords
a tor is a high rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: Someone describes a route via a large hill and a small Dickens character in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little Dickensian' points to Little Nell, giving just NELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritornello is a recurring instrumental section in a piece of music, so it is a musical passage.

clue.text: Blimey! Supermarket no longer selling ice cream

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
Netto was a discount supermarket chain that closed its UK stores

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed that the shop has stopped stocking their favourite ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: NETTO was a discount supermarket chain in Britain, now gone, hence 'no longer selling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornetto is a branded cone of ice cream topped with chocolate and nuts.

clue.text: Cheat to get violin

definitions.meaning: to cheat is to swindle, as in fiddling the accounts
an informal name for a violin

explanation.surface: A con artist's plan to acquire a valuable violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: swindling someone, and the folk name for the stringed instrument.

clue.text: That's my lot, eaten by swimmer of evil intent

indicators.note: the phrase is swallowed by the swimmer, so it goes inside that word's letters

parts.note: a fish is a creature that swims
saying that's my lot means I end, I have finished

explanation.surface: Someone resigns themselves to being devoured by a malevolent sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's my lot' is read as I END, which sits inside FISH after its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devilishly cruel has the wicked purpose of a demon, hence being of evil intent.

clue.text: Mad days out involving Roger in sitcom

indicators.note: the rearranged days take in the extra letter within them
out signals the letters are disordered, as in something put out of place

parts.note: R is Roger in radio signalling, meaning received

explanation.surface: Crazy days off featuring someone called Roger, in a TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes DADSAMY from MAD DAYS, and R goes inside before the M. Dad's Army is a classic British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad's Army is a long-running BBC comedy series, so it is an example of a situation comedy.

clue.text: Islander supplying vessel for underage drinker?

indicators.note: the vessel is for the drinker, so the drinker's word comes before it

parts.note: a minor is someone below the legal age, here for drinking
a can is a container for drinks

explanation.surface: Someone asks who provides a drinks can for a teenager who should not be drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A Minorcan comes from Minorca, one of the Balearic Islands, so is an islander.

clue.text: Revolutionary with fish head to cook

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: the head of the word fish is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rebel leader using a fish head in his cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a kitchen.

clue.text: Crazy for health food

definitions.meaning: almonds and walnuts are sold as healthy snacks

explanation.surface: Someone is obsessed with wholefoods.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: slang for insane, and the edible kernels sold in wholefood shops.

clue.text: Increase affection for organ stop first

indicators.note: the word for stop is placed first, ahead of the organ, though the clue gives it later

parts.note: end means stop or finish
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Instructions for a church organist, pulling out a stop first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ stop' looks like the musical knob, but organ and stop are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone or something beloved is to raise others' fondness towards it.

clue.text: Gloomy start to musical performance?

definitions.meaning: the conductor's downward stroke marking the first beat of a bar starts the playing

explanation.surface: A sombre opening to a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Pessimistic in mood, and the accented first beat a conductor signals with a downward stroke.

clue.text: Strongly opposed to good person having copped it twice before

indicators.note: the dying twice comes before the good person, so those letters lead

parts.note: to have copped it is to have died, so twice means dead again
ST, saint, is a crossword stock for a good person

explanation.surface: Someone firmly objects to a decent person who has been killed twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copped it' is British slang for died.
explanation.definitionFit: Being implacably hostile to something is an idiom for strong opposition.

clue.text: Not obviously ill, wanting mother never to meet

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word for mother is removed

parts.note: showing no symptoms while carrying an illness
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A patient who seems well and does not want their mother ever to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like desire but means missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, an asymptotic curve approaches a line ever more closely but never touches it.

clue.text: Inactive bone in heap

indicators.note: the bone is placed in the heap, inside its letters

parts.note: a mound is a heap or pile
a rib is a bone of the chest

explanation.surface: A neglected bone lies in a pile.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means near death or stagnant, so something effectively dormant or inactive.

clue.text: Second comedian — pedant!

parts.note: a comedian is one who tickles an audience

explanation.surface: A second comic is dismissed as a nitpicker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact rules and details, as a pedant does.

clue.text: Speak about march returning sooner or later

indicators.note: the word for speak goes about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: returning means the protest word is read backwards

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Speaking about a march that will come back eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: At some unspecified future time, that is eventually.

clue.text: Vessel to drive, empty, at reasonable lick

indicators.note: emptying a word leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: a canter is a moderate pace, a reasonable speed

explanation.surface: Driving a boat at a decent speed with nothing aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' removes the middle of drive, leaving DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass container for wine or spirits, so a vessel in the sense of receptacle.

clue.text: Prospect of thug securing nothing satisfactory

indicators.note: the thug holds the other pieces securely within

parts.note: a lout is an uncouth aggressive person
O represents zero
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A hooligan's chances of getting anything worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or outlook, as in a poor outlook for the future, matches prospect.

clue.text: Playing piccolo, Lara becomes compulsive swearer

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lara turns foul-mouthed whenever she picks up the flute.
explanation.definitionFit: Coprolalia is involuntary use of obscene language, as in some Tourette's, so a sufferer swears compulsively.

clue.text: Manifestation of a French department receiving thanks

indicators.note: the department receives the word for thanks inside it

parts.note: Var is a department in Provence
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A regional French government office is sent a thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the incarnation or embodiment of a deity or idea.

clue.text: Member's got nearly nowhere

indicators.note: nearly means just short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: limbo is a state of being nowhere, in neither place

explanation.surface: A club member has made almost no progress.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body.

clue.text: Shape of toilet turning round first

indicators.note: the round letter comes first, before the other piece

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: turning means the toilet word is read backwards

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a toilet

explanation.surface: Describing the outline of a lavatory seat when going round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-shaped figure is a geometric form or outline.

clue.text: Franklin, say — contributor with poles reversed

indicators.note: south swapped for north, as when magnetic poles flip

parts.note: an investor contributes money to a venture

explanation.surface: Benjamin Franklin as a backer who flipped magnetic poles, nodding to his electrical experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin devised the lightning rod and bifocals, an example of a creator of new devices.

clue.text: America turned into one of its states — not smart!

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation goes into the state's letters

parts.note: Cal is short for California, one of the US states

indicators.note: turned means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: USA, United States of America

explanation.surface: A country morphs into one of its own regions, a comedown in elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal dress is the opposite of smart attire.

clue.text: Northern European keeping the French dancing

indicators.note: the European word keeps the article inside it

parts.note: Baltic describes the northern European region by the Baltic Sea
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A northern European holding on to French people as they dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Balletic means graceful in the manner of ballet, hence relating to dancing.

clue.text: Indulge Prince and Queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a regal abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Royalty being spoilt rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify someone's wishes or weaknesses is to humour or indulge them.
